title: live-verify.mjs and its generated summary.md both state that POST /ask 'appends one real jobs ledger row' -- the real figure is 20-26 rows per run, and it is non-deterministic between runs; the false count is baked into every evidence artifact the tool produces, in a unit whose entire claim is that disclosures are true

fix_direction: Do not hand-wave a constant. title: STUB/MISSING checks are pinned to the exact current status code, so implementing a route inverts its verdict to FAIL -- shipping GET /health (404 -> 200) or GET /search (501 -> 200) would break the verification suite, making the protocol penalise progress

title: DIRTY-TREE does not affect overall or the exit code, so a run whose own summary says it is 'not valid as final acceptance evidence' still emits `overall: PASS` and exit 0 -- any CI or agent keying on the exit code cannot distinguish attributable from non-attributable evidence
evidence: scripts/live-verify.mjs:223-227 (overall is FAIL if any FAIL, else INCONCLUSIVE if any INCONCLUSIVE, else PASS -- DIRTY-TREE is in neither ladder) and :265 (`process.exit(overall === 'FAIL' ? 2 : overall === 'INCONCLUSIVE' ? 3 : 0)`). Both of my runs printed DIRTY-TREE at preflight and still ended `overall: PASS`, EXIT=0. NOTE: I explicitly tested the masking question the dispatch asked and DIRTY-TREE does NOT mask a real failure -- it is assigned at exactly one check (preflight attribution) and cannot suppress any other check's FAIL; that part of the design is sound.
fix_direction: Give it its own exit code (e.g. 4) or render the headline as `overall: PASS (DIRTY-TREE -- not attributable to <sha>)`, so a machine consumer sees the caveat the human-readable line already carries. Secondary, lower priority: each run's own evidence folder becomes an untracked entry that the NEXT run counts as a dirty file (I observed the count go 10 -> 11 between my two runs), so the tool slowly dirties the tree it measures unless evidence is committed after every run.
checker_verdict: cycle 2 PASS - independently reproduced as fixed (qa/verdicts/live-verify-protocol.md)

title: The fifth layer: `git ls-files --error-unmatch` proves only that the evidence PATH is tracked, never that its CONTENT matches the committed blob - so editing the already-committed preflight.json in place inflates the headline 20.2% -> 39.5% with --check AND pnpm lint:structure both exit 0 and NO uncommitted banner
evidence: Executed by checker: rewriting every count in the already-committed qa/evidence/live-2026-09-07-01-58-41/preflight.json to 4242 (no new folder, no commit, same internal stamp) yields 'wrote docs/PROGRESS.md - 39.5% adjusted / 50% machine-derived' exit 0; 'node scripts/catalogue-score.mjs --check' -> 'OK: docs/PROGRESS.md is current (39.5% of 57 features)' exit 0; 'pnpm lint:structure' exit 0 at 39.5%; NO UNCOMMITTED banner is printed because isTracked() returns true; probe fingerprint unchanged. +19.3 points, the same magnitude as ISS-035, defeating the very gate built to close ISS-035. Root cause scripts/lib/catalogue.mjs:148-155 isTracked(): 'git ls-files --error-unmatch <path>' is a path-existence query, not a content query. This directly falsifies the manifest's disclosed ceiling ('what it now costs is a visible commit with a changed sha') - the actual cost is an uncommitted working-tree edit, i.e. exactly the same cost as the original ISS-035 attack.
fix_direction: Replace isTracked() with a content-attribution check using machinery already imported: `git diff --quiet HEAD -- <path>` (exit 0 = clean) or hash `git show HEAD:<path>` and compare to the working-tree hash already computed. Then the printed sha is genuinely attributable to a commit and the --check gate means what it says. Contract I11 (added by checker cycle 3, effective next cycle).

title: The evidence content sha printed into docs/PROGRESS.md is line-ending dependent, so on a fresh clone (core.autocrlf=true, the default on Windows and set in this repo) --check reports STALE and lint:structure goes red with zero edits
evidence: Measured by checker: the committed blob for qa/evidence/live-2026-09-07-01-58-41/preflight.json is LF, 804 bytes (git cat-file -s 72f6690a = 804). After `git checkout -- <that path>` git materialises it as CRLF, 840 bytes, and the sha printed in the doc changes 5f7ed1c0d434 -> 3a73c60dcc6d, making docs/PROGRESS.md byte-different (sha256 1C028F7E... -> 5A8443C2...). With the evidence so materialised, 'node scripts/catalogue-score.mjs --check' -> 'STALE: docs/PROGRESS.md differs from a fresh regeneration' exit 1, hence lint:structure red on an untouched clone. `git config core.autocrlf` = true in this repo. Regenerating 'fixes' it locally but produces a diff that flips straight back on an LF machine - a ping-pong diff between platforms. Note this compounds a PRE-EXISTING instance of the same class (git also warns that docs/PROGRESS.md itself is LF-in-worktree / CRLF-on-checkout, and generate() joins with \n), so I1 byte-for-byte re-derivability was already platform-dependent before this unit; this unit adds a second, independent CRLF-sensitive input.
fix_direction: Hash the LF-normalised content (raw.replace(/\r\n/g,'\n')) before printing the sha, or read the blob via `git show HEAD:<path>` so the sha is the committed bytes rather than the checkout's. Separately consider a .gitattributes entry pinning qa/evidence/**/*.json and docs/PROGRESS.md to `text eol=lf` so the whole class is closed.
checker_verdict: Closed by unit evidence-trust-by-content cycle 1 for the defect as charged (the NEW, second CRLF-sensitive input). Verified by forcing the real materialisation, not a simulation: rm the evidence file then 'git checkout --' it, with core.autocrlf=true confirmed at C:/Program Files/Git/etc/gitconfig. Real checkout = CRLF (36 CR), raw sha 3a73c60dcc6d; LF = 0 CR, raw sha 5f7ed1c0d434 - exactly the pair this issue was filed on - and the CANONICAL fingerprint is 78a2fc2b0743 in BOTH, with 'git diff --quiet HEAD' exit 0 and --check exit 0 in both. Also invariant under reversed key order and a 4-space reindent; moves to ebc3ae1f17e5 when one count changes (turns 2118->2119). fingerprint() at scripts/lib/evidence.mjs:76-82 hashes canonical parsed content (stamp + key-sorted counts). Contract verify step 14 satisfied. The PRE-EXISTING half this issue explicitly scoped out (docs/PROGRESS.md is itself CRLF-materialised on checkout, so --check reports STALE exit 1 on an untouched clone) SURVIVES and is refiled as ISS-043.

title: A malformed or BOM-prefixed preflight.json is silently skipped, so the scorer can quietly fall back to stale evidence with no warning
evidence: Observed by checker while building an attack fixture: a preflight.json written with a UTF-8 BOM (bytes EF BB BF, as Windows PowerShell 5.1 `Out-File -Encoding utf8` produces) makes JSON.parse throw and is swallowed by `try { pre = JSON.parse(raw); } catch { continue; }` at scripts/lib/catalogue.mjs:122. The run was silently ignored and the score was computed from the older evidence with no message at all. Fails SAFE here (it lowers rather than inflates, and the doc names whichever file it did use), which is why this is low and not high - but a newest legitimate run that is unreadable for any reason silently scores from stale data.
fix_direction: Strip a leading BOM before JSON.parse, and print a one-line warning naming any live-* candidate that could not be parsed instead of continuing in silence. Matches the sweep's silent-failure rule (a catch that swallows an error the caller needed).

title: The SIXTH layer: .goal/catalogue.json is a score-raising input with NO trust check of any kind, so editing it without committing moves the headline 20.2% -> 62.3% (+42.1 points, more than double the ISS-037 lever) with --check, pnpm lint:structure and all 33 tests green
evidence: Executed by checker from a clean tree (git status showed .goal/catalogue.json unmodified beforehand). Repointing the 19 probe-less feature rows at a populated collection (probes:{collections:['turns']}, 2118 docs) and nulling out the 11 manual downgrades yields: 'node scripts/catalogue-score.mjs' -> 'wrote docs/PROGRESS.md - 62.3% adjusted / 62.3% machine-derived, 57 features' exit 0; 'node scripts/catalogue-score.mjs --check' -> 'OK: docs/PROGRESS.md is current (62.3% of 57 features)' exit 0; 'pnpm lint:structure' exit 0; 'node --test scripts/catalogue.test.mjs' 19/19 pass. Split into independent halves: repointing the probe-less rows alone = 53.5% (+33.3 pts, --check exit 0); nulling the manual downgrades alone = 28.9% (+8.7 pts, --check exit 0). Same shape as ISS-037: trust applied to one input class (qa/evidence/*/preflight.json now demands content-vs-HEAD) and not the other (.goal/catalogue.json has not even a path check). I5 does not stop it - the probe fingerprint DID change (9acec0d56307 -> 6b58726d4979) but it is printed into the document the same run regenerates and nothing compares it to anything, so it is reviewability with no reviewer. I2 does not stop the second half either: DELETING a manual downgrade is not an upgrade relative to the derived verdict, so the one-directional upgrade guard has nothing to object to. Bound: the machine ceiling with probes repointed is 62.3%, so this cannot manufacture 100% - but it comfortably manufactures 'the product is two-thirds built', which is exactly the false statement this unit exists to prevent.
fix_direction: Apply the I11 treatment to .goal/catalogue.json: call trustOf(root, '.goal/catalogue.json') in generate(), print its trust state + content fingerprint into docs/PROGRESS.md next to the probe fingerprint, and make --check refuse (exit 2) when it is anything but committed - exactly the gate the evidence file already has. Consider also treating the REMOVAL of a manual downgrade as a score-raising change reported alongside upgrades. Contract I13 (added by checker this cycle, effective next cycle).

title: Trust is not pinned to HEAD by any test: rewriting 'git diff --quiet HEAD --' to 'git diff --quiet --' (working tree vs INDEX) survives the whole suite, and would let a bare 'git add' restore the full +19.3-point lever with no banner
evidence: Mutation executed by checker. scripts/lib/evidence.mjs:44 git(root, ['diff','--quiet','HEAD','--',relPath]) -> git(root, ['diff','--quiet','--',relPath]): 'node --test scripts/catalogue.test.mjs' stays at 19 pass / 0 fail. Exploit confirmed with the mutation in place: tamper every zero count in the committed qa/evidence/live-2026-09-07-01-58-41/preflight.json to 4242, then 'git add -- <that path>' (NO commit) -> 'node scripts/catalogue-score.mjs' writes 39.5%, grep -c for 'EDITED SINCE COMMIT|UNCOMMITTED' in docs/PROGRESS.md = 0 (no banner at all), 'node scripts/catalogue-score.mjs --check' -> 'OK: docs/PROGRESS.md is current (39.5% of 57 features)' exit 0, tests still 19/19. The suite tamper fixture (scripts/catalogue.test.mjs:140) writes the file without staging it, so index-vs-HEAD is indistinguishable to it. The SHIPPED code is correct - this is a coverage gap that would let a plausible simplifying refactor silently reopen the attack, the exact ISS-030/ISS-038 failure mode. Contract I11 says committed must mean the CONTENT compared to the committed blob; staged-not-committed is neither.
fix_direction: Add one test to the existing throwaway-git-repo helper (gitRepoWithEvidence, scripts/catalogue.test.mjs:125): tamper the evidence file, 'git add' it WITHOUT committing, and assert trustOf(root, rel) === 'modified'. About fifteen lines against a fixture that already exists. Contract I12.

title: docs/PROGRESS.md is itself CRLF-materialised on checkout, so --check still reports STALE (exit 1) and pnpm lint:structure still goes red on an untouched clone - the pre-existing half of the ISS-039 class that the evidence-fingerprint fix does not reach
evidence: Measured by checker. 'git config --show-origin core.autocrlf' = true (C:/Program Files/Git/etc/gitconfig), and git warns 'in the working copy of docs/PROGRESS.md, LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it'; the same warning on the evidence file was confirmed real by rm + 'git checkout --', which materialised it as CRLF (36 CR). generate() joins with a bare newline and writeFileSync emits LF, while scripts/catalogue-score.mjs:121-122 compares the on-disk bytes to that LF text with 'committed !== text'. Converting docs/PROGRESS.md to CRLF (exactly what a fresh clone produces) gives 'node scripts/catalogue-score.mjs --check' -> 'STALE: docs/PROGRESS.md differs from a fresh regeneration' exit 1, hence lint:structure red with zero edits. ISS-039 own text scoped this half out as pre-existing ('this unit adds a SECOND, independent CRLF-sensitive input'); that second input is now fixed, this first one is not. Fails safe (red, not green) so it is medium not high - but a gate that is red on a clean clone is a gate people learn to bypass.
fix_direction: Add a .gitattributes entry pinning docs/PROGRESS.md and qa/evidence/**/*.json to 'text eol=lf' (closes the whole class at the repo level, and was already the second half of the ISS-039 fix_direction), or LF-normalise both sides of the 'committed !== text' comparison at scripts/catalogue-score.mjs:122.
